'''Roger Paquin''' (born July 24, 1947) is a Quebec politician. He served as the member for [[Saint-Jean (provincial electoral district)|Saint-Jean]] in the [[Quebec National Assembly]] as a member of the [[Parti Québécois]] from 1994 until 2003.

==Biography==

Paquin was born in [[Montreal]], He earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree, a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in Biology, and a [[master's degree]] in [[science]] [[didactics]] from the [[Université de Montréal]]. He obtained a certificate in [[Mind map|cognitive style mapping]] from [[Oakland Community College]] and a certificate in [[project management]] from the [[Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières]].

Paquin was a Professor of [[Biology]] at the [[Cégep de Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu]] and served as a professional in the General Directorate of Collegial Education at the [[Quebec Ministry of Education]].

==Political career==

Paquin served as secretary and later the president of his local PQ riding executive. He later became Chairman of the National Council of the provincial party. He ran in [[Saint-Jean (provincial electoral district)|Saint-Jean]] in [[1994 Quebec general election|1994]]; the election ended in a tie between him and Liberal incumbent [[Michel Charbonneau]] with 16,536 votes each. A by-election was called and a month later Paquin won by 532 votes.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/elections/quebecvotes2014/ridings/view/riding-104 Saint-Jean]</ref> He was re-elected without any difficulty in [[1998 Quebec general election|1998]].

He was Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister responsible for the [[Montérégie]] Region in the [[Lucien Bouchard|Bouchard government]]. He then became Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of the Environment, and then the Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of the Environment and Water in both the Bouchard and the [[Bernard Landry|Landry]] governments.

Paquin sought re-election in [[2003 Quebec general election|2003]], and lost to Liberal [[Jean-Pierre Paquin]] (no relation).<ref>[http://www.assnat.qc.ca/en/deputes/paquin-roger-4751/biographie.html Roger Paquin Quebec National Assembly Biography]</ref>
